subject: chemistry
title: Concentration in g/dm³
key_idea: The concentration of a solution is the mass of solute in a given volume of solution. It is measured in grams per cubic decimetre (g/dm³). A concentrated solution has more solute in the same volume than a dilute solution.

blocks.text: A solution is made by dissolving a solute in a solvent. This section covers how concentration compares solutions.

items.meaning: The solute and the solvent together.
The mass of solute in a given volume of solution, such as g/dm³.
A dilute solution has a low ratio of solute to volume. A concentrated solution has a high ratio.

items: Putting more solute in the same volume makes a solution more concentrated.
Putting the same solute in a bigger volume makes it more dilute.
Dilute and concentrated describe the amount of solute. Strong and weak describe how far an acid ionises, which is a different idea.
Concentration = how much solute in a volume of solution.
More solute in the same volume means more concentrated.
Dilute and concentrated are not the same as weak and strong.

blocks.text: The volume must be in dm³. Change cm³ to dm³ first by dividing by 1000.

blocks.label: Concentration
blocks.formula: concentration (g/dm³) = mass of solute (g) ÷ volume of solution (dm³)
where: To change cm³ to dm³, divide by 1000.

items.text: 28.4 g of sodium sulfate is dissolved to make 250 cm³ of solution. 250 ÷ 1000 = 0.250 dm³.

diagram.alt: Practise calculating concentration in g/dm³ from a mass and a volume in cm³.
diagram.question: **{m} g** of sodium chloride is dissolved in water to make **{V} cm³** of solution. Calculate the concentration in g/dm³.

items: Divide cm³ by 1000 to get dm³.
Check the number of significant figures asked for.

blocks.text: Rearrange the equation to find the mass of solute or the volume of solution. Keep the volume in dm³ until the end.

blocks.label: Mass of solute
where: Convert the volume to dm³ first.

items.text: Barium chloride, 21 g/dm³, in 25 cm³. 25 ÷ 1000 = 0.025 dm³.
21 × 0.025 = 0.525 g, which is 0.53 g to 2 significant figures.
A calcium chloride solution is 12 g/dm³. Volume containing 9.0 g = 9.0 ÷ 12 = 0.75 dm³.

items: Change other units too. 125 mg is 125 ÷ 1000 = 0.125 g.
A mean concentration comes from the mean mass, divided by the volume in dm³.
Convert all units before you calculate.

checks.q: What is the unit of concentration used in this note?
45 g of glucose is dissolved in water to make 150 cm³ of solution. Calculate the concentration in g/dm³.
Calculate the mass of solute in 800 cm³ of a solution with a concentration of 258 g/dm³.
checks.a: 800 ÷ 1000 = 0.8 dm³. 0.8 × 258 = 206.4 g, which is 206 g to 3 significant figures.

worked_example.question:
Four samples of sea water were tested. Each sample had a volume of 10.0 cm³.

Sea water sample A: 0.35 g of dissolved solids
Sea water sample B: 0.37 g of dissolved solids
Sea water sample C: 0.33 g of dissolved solids
Sea water sample D: 0.34 g of dissolved solids

Calculate the mean concentration of dissolved solids in 10.0 cm³ samples of sea water A, B, C and D.

Use the equation: mean concentration of dissolved solids (g/dm³) = mean mass of dissolved solids (g) ÷ volume of sample (dm³)

Give your answer in g/dm³.
worked_example.tip: You can also find each concentration (35, 37, 33, 34) and then take the mean.

worked_example.question:
The sodium sulfate solution was made by dissolving 28.4 g of sodium sulfate in water to make 250 cm³ of solution.

Calculate the concentration of this solution in g dm⁻³.

Give your answer to three significant figures.
worked_example.tip: The final mark needs three significant figures.

worked_example.question:
Barium chloride solid is toxic if swallowed and harmful if inhaled.

Barium chloride solutions with concentrations of 21 g / dm³ are suitable for experiments in school.

Calculate the mass of barium chloride that should be dissolved in 25 cm³ of water to make a solution with a concentration of 21 g / dm³.

Use the equation: concentration = mass ÷ volume

Give your answer to 2 significant figures.
worked_example.tip: You can instead convert 21 g/dm³ to 0.021 g/cm³ and multiply by 25.

worked_example.question:
Magnesium sulfate is a salt. Magnesium sulfate is soluble in water.

The solubility of a salt is the mass of the salt, in g, that dissolves in 100 cm³ of water at a specified temperature.

Plan an investigation to determine the solubility of magnesium sulfate in water at 50 °C. Your plan must include how the solubility of magnesium sulfate, in g per 100 cm³ of water, can be found.

You are provided with solid magnesium sulfate, distilled water and common laboratory apparatus.
answer_points: Measure 100 cm³ of water with a measuring cylinder and put it in a beaker
Heat the water to 50 °C and keep it at that temperature
Add magnesium sulfate in excess, or in portions until no more dissolves, and stir
Filter off the undissolved solid, or use the known mass of solid that was added
Use the measurements to calculate the solubility: mass dissolved = mass added − mass of undissolved solid, in g per 100 cm³ of water
worked_example.tip: Any six marking points score. The plan needs a method for how the solubility is found.

blocks.text: Concentration can be measured in g/dm³ or in mol/dm³. This note uses g/dm³.

items.meaning: A substance that dissolves a solute.
A solution containing the maximum amount of solute dissolved in the solvent at a given temperature.
The solid that remains after evaporation, distillation, filtration or a similar process.
The liquid or solution that has passed through a filter.

items: mol/dm³ is the number of moles of solute in 1 dm³ of solution.
Solubility is often given as the mass in g that dissolves in 100 cm³ of water at a stated temperature.
